versions.description: Audit fixes: FedoraKDE move recorded, relocatable harness launcher, thermal-doc correction, battery unit, sleep enforcement documented

features.title: OOM containment: harness.slice + oom-guard + launcher
features.notes: L1 harness.slice 18G/4G with ManagedOOMMemoryPressure=auto, L2 omit on WezTerm/Plasma via 10 s guard, launcher raises oom_score_adj=900 inside the scope. Proven in production: kernel cgroup OOM killed nocowboy inside harness.slice, terminal survived.

features.title: Harness launcher independent of the external drive
features.notes: oom-guard.sh now installs harness-run.sh into ~/.local/lib/no-cowboy/ and links ~/.local/bin/harness to that copy; a symlink into the repo died when the external drive was unmounted (reviewer follow-up #2).

features.title: Correct thermal analysis: display topology is the idle-power driver
features.notes: fbdev=1 is a driver default on nvidia-open 615, not a GRUB flag; DP-1 + HDMI-A-1 are on the dGPU so it never idles (35-52 W). Balanced profile is not the quiet profile on this EC (fan blow-up). Doc now carries the measured chain and the card2 (DP-2/DP-3) test.

features.title: Battery charge limit unit uses asusctl (not BAT1 sysfs)
features.notes: systemd/battery-charge-limit.service wrote to /sys/class/power_supply/BAT1/charge_control_end_threshold, which does not exist on this model. Rewritten to asusctl battery limit 80 via asusd. Not installed by default; enabling it applies the 80% cap.

features.title: Enforce the sleep decision (mask sleep targets)
features.notes: SLEEP-WAKE-ISSUES.md says sleep is disabled, but the targets are static, not masked. Root step documented in the doc: systemctl mask sleep.target suspend.target hibernate.target hybrid-sleep.target. Needs a human with sudo.

features.title: Display topology measured; refresh is the only GPU-idle lever
features.notes: Measured 2026-11-10: both external ports are wired to the dGPU (USB-C enumerates as card1-DP-1; iGPU DP-2/DP-3 are disconnected), so there is no iGPU route. Refresh is the only lever: 144/144 Hz → 33.6 W P3; 60/60 Hz → 26.0 W P5 (~7.5 W, one P-state). Fans did not drop because the CPU package was 86–92 °C under the AI harness. 144 Hz restored after the test.

features.title: SYSTEM-STATE.md and roadmap.json reflect 2026-11-10
features.notes: The state doc was frozen at 2024-12-30 (kernel 6.18.2-zen2); a verified current-state section now precedes the historical record, and the roadmap is no longer empty.

features.title: Record the FedoraKDE kit move out of the repo
features.notes: The kit lives at LinuxDCO/misc_os/FedoraKDE next to the NixOS kit (38 files, identical content plus assets/). The misleading 'refresh' commit was rewritten to describe the move.

features.title: CPU quota on harness.slice (thermal guard)
features.notes: CPUQuota=400% + CPUWeight=50 in ~/.config/systemd/user/harness.slice.d/zz-cpu.conf; persistent, applied live with set-property (no slice restart). Measured 97->71 C when the burst paused; the hotspot itself is single-core boost, so this limits parallelism, not the peak.

features.title: Sustained PL1 cap (root) to attack the 97 C hotspot
features.notes: scripts/tools/thermal-guard.sh cap --pl1 45 writes ASUS ppt_pl1_spl (watts, ABI range 5-250; the sysfs read shows the driver default 5, not the live limit) and installs asus-thermal-cap.service. PL2 untouched. Gate: throttle ms/min drops and a timed build regresses <10%. Needs root.

features.title: Adopt the workstation architecture protocol, corrected against measurements
features.notes: docs/ARCHITECTURE-PROTOCOL.md replaces the draft: OOMScoreAdjust=-500 is impossible unprivileged and rejected by systemd 262.1 on scopes (and oomd ignores it) -> omit + in-scope score 900; MemoryHigh rejected (livelock) -> hard MemoryMax; both external ports are on the dGPU so there is no iGPU routing; LTS installed 6.18.58-1 with DKMS, default unchanged; no pacman interceptor (sudo secure_path) - prepare/install split is the guardrail.

features.title: Portable workstation profile (bootstrap.sh) with hardware detection
features.notes: Single entrypoint instead of a distro: detect (DMI, ASUS WMI, DRM card vendors, dracut, oomd, zram, snapshots, systemd, battery) then layer1 (oom-guard, CPU quota, /usr/local staging, LTS) and layer2 (profile policy check, PL1 cap, battery unit, display map) only on a recognised machine. Idempotent, no packages/upgrades/reboots, rootless by default with exact root commands printed; --dry-run, status and uninstall included.

features.title: Semi-automatic Friday upgrade with recurring reminders
features.notes: timer 21:55 Europe/Moscow -> prepare-run.sh notifies the active session, sleeps WARN_BEFORE=300s, stages with update-engine prepare (mirrors, -Syy, snapshot, download), then asks via kdialog --yesno (geometry 760x240, timeout PROMPT_TIMEOUT=600 -> Later). Only 'Install now' hands over to update-now.sh. MODE=auto|semi|stage in /etc/garuda-restore/update.conf; GUI is reached from the root service through logind (runuser + XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/DBUS/WAYLAND_DISPLAY). No active session => no install. update-prompt.timer (every 5 min, inert unless due) calls prompt-run.sh: MODE=semi only, staged/pending>0, no lock/engine, then the cadence: first reminder 1 h after the staging prompt, then every 3 h until install or the next Friday. State in /var/lib/garuda-restore/prompt.state (LAST_PROMPT, DECLINES). 'Install now' hands over to update-now.sh. --dry-run and NOCOWBOY_STATE/NOCOWBOY_LOG test hooks validate the cadence without GUI.
